summary: The bad() entry point reads an integer from a network socket and passes it directly to the HashMap(int initialCapacity) constructor, allowing an attacker-controlled value to drive an uncontrolled, potentially huge memory allocation (CWE-789). The fix validates the value against a sane positive upper bound before using it as the initial capacity, so legitimate capacity values still size the HashMap as intended while out-of-range or attacker-inflated values no longer trigger an unbounded allocation.
